final_message:
I couldn't reproduce this, so I haven't changed anything. In this repo, `slugify('Hello,  World!')` already returns `'hello-world'`, and all 5 tests pass.

The function in `src/slugify.py:4` collapses each run of non-alphanumeric characters into a single `-` (the regex `[^a-z0-9]+`). It then strips leading and trailing dashes. The output `'hello---world-'` would come from an older version. That version probably replaced each character separately, with a pattern like `[^a-z0-9]` without the `+`, and didn't strip the ends.

The users may be running an older release or a different copy of the code. Check which version they have installed. If you can share where they see the bad output, such as a stack trace, a package version, or a different file, I can look there.

I can also add a regression test for `'Hello,  World!'` to `tests/test_slugify.py` so this can't come back. Say so if you want it.
